result.title: Same Operation, Different Permission: Evaluating Whether Guardrails Honor Authorization
result.summary: As language-model agents write code, move money and change records on behalf of users, deciding whether an action is authorized has become a central safety problem. Guardrails are often placed in front of these actions, yet few evaluations ask whether their decisions follow authorization: blocking unauthorized actions while still allowing the same actions under valid permission. We introduce \bench{}, a benchmark that contrasts authorization evidence for the same operation in its language track. It combines expert-annotated natural-language scenarios with executed and verified operations, plus externally sourced native-policy requests. \bench{} checks each decision for correctness, usability and resulting effect, and tracks each request across guardrail changes. Our experiments show that many blocked operations stem from failed reviews, not correct denials. Repairing the output format restores usable decisions but changes which authorized requests are honored, and adding a second reviewer removes some errors while rejecting valid authorization. Guardrails should therefore be evaluated on both the unauthorized actions they stop and the authorized actions they let through.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一个基准，用同一操作在「有无授权」下的对照场景（专家标注情景＋已验证操作＋外部原生策略请求）检验防护栏的判定是否真正依据授权，并按正确性、可用性与实际效果评估，还追踪防护栏改动后的请求迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「同一输入、不同权限证据」的对照式评测与逐项检查判定是否由证据支撑，可能为 LVR 中「推理是否真正使用视觉/任务必要证据、如何做贡献分配」提供评价思路，但领域相距较远，联系仅供核查。
